elements.element: No liquidated damages are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 7.9 still requires breach-triggered extended payment charges calculated under a predetermined formula until payment. Because Subparagraph 7.8 is not provided, the operative text does not establish that these charges are merely compensatory rather than a liquidated amount; the margin comment cannot supply that limitation.

elements.element: No penalties are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 7.9 retains mandatory late-payment charges without an operative non-penalty or compensatory limitation, and Section 23.2 terminates the defaulting Party's rights while broadly preserving its obligations under the Agreement. The pro-rata credit and reimbursement language does not eliminate the possibility of continuing payment obligations after rights and capacity are reclaimed.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer is capped at three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Section 23.2 terminates the defaulting Party's rights and party status upon reclamation but states that reclamation does not relieve that Party from its obligations under the Agreement. The clause contains no three-month cap, and the broad survival language prevents the absence of a termination-related charge from being demonstrated.

elements.element: The capped early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 7.9 separately imposes formula-based extended payment charges for late payment, and Section 23.2 broadly preserves obligations following termination. Neither provision limits Customer's sole liquidated liability to a capped early-termination fee.

result.reason: The redline removes the express 300% multiplier and mitigates forfeiture through pro-rata credit and reimbursement, but it does not operatively eliminate liquidated or penal charges. The referenced Subparagraph 7.8 rate is unavailable, and Section 23.2 preserves obligations after all rights terminate without a three-month cap. The edits are targeted and leave unrelated mechanics intact, but they do not reach either complete position; the undefined pro-rata methodology and potentially overlapping credit and reimbursement remedies also reduce drafting precision.
